thesis: SONY is up ~17.9% over 60 days (close_60d_ago 21.16 -> latest_close 24.94), but the gain tracks a broad AI/semiconductor investment narrative -- a $6.3B TSMC-Sony image-sensor plant JV in Kumamoto, an AI facility-maintenance deal with Saudi Aramco, and a sector-wide chip/AI rally -- rather than one Sony-specific confirmed event. Company-specific news in the window is otherwise neutral to mixed: a $476.6k insider share sale (Aug 17) and PlayStation's Horizon Hunters Gathering being reworked after negative player feedback. Sony Music (a Sony unit) also sued Anthropic over copyright, but as plaintiff seeking damages, not a liability exposure.
invalidation: If the broader AI/semiconductor rally cools or the announced JV/AI deals fail to translate into disclosed financial impact, expect the move to unwind disproportionately to any Sony-specific news.

thesis: HOOD jumped ~15% today on volume 2.78x its 30-day average, but a sourced Benzinga market recap states the move "tracks bitcoin's 4.6% advance and the softer dollar" with "neither name carrying company-specific news in the tape" (grouping HOOD with other crypto-linked stocks) -- i.e. the sharp move is explicitly described as crypto-beta/sentiment-driven rather than a Robinhood-specific event. This week's several analyst upgrades (Morgan Stanley to Overweight/$150 PT, Piper Sandler $145, Scotiabank initiation at $136) are opinions, not confirmed events, and the stock is already ~21% above its 20-day moving average after the spike. Underlying legal risk continues: the Ninth Circuit ruled against Robinhood's sports event-contracts (finding them not federally regulated swaps), which Robinhood plans to appeal, while a related case (New Jersey v. Kalshi) awaits a cert decision on whether the Supreme Court takes up the circuit split.
invalidation: If Bitcoin/crypto sentiment reverses, or the appeal on sports event contracts fails and forces Robinhood to pull the product from more states, the case for chasing today's move weakens further.

thesis: SU is up ~24.4% over 60 days (close_60d_ago 54.91 -> latest_close 68.28) and sits just 2.9% below its 52-week high, on volume 2.97x the 30-day average. This follows a confirmed Q2 beat (adjusted EPS CA$3.23 vs CA$3.04 est.; revenue CA$19.0B vs CA$12.75B a year earlier, reported Aug. 4) plus broader crude-oil price strength through the period (WTI/Brent both up in the same window per sector coverage); Morgan Stanley also upgraded the stock to Overweight (Aug 19, opinion not a confirmed event). A routine, board-led CEO succession was announced Aug. 6 (CEO Rich Kruger to Executive Vice Chair in April 2027, EVP Peter Zebedee to succeed him), not tied to any disclosed operational problem. With both a real earnings catalyst and a sector-wide commodity tailwind contributing, no single driver is clearly dominant.
invalidation: A pullback in crude oil prices, or a miss on the next quarterly report, would undercut the current momentum and call the thesis into question.
